jobs.title: Software Engineer with an Affinity for Livestock Farming
jobs.description:
Your job

Are you a software engineer who looks beyond just code? Do you have a practical background or strong affinity with livestock farming and do you want to use your technical skills to make the agricultural sector smarter and more sustainable? Then we are looking for you.

What will you do?

As a software engineer, you will work on innovative digital solutions for livestock farming. Think of simulation programs to perform scenario analyses, applications for data collection and analysis and management systems for livestock farms (digital twins). You translate practical questions into smart software and work closely with colleagues from both IT and agricultural background.

Your Tasks

developing and maintaining software (e.g. web applications, dashboards or other software tools);
translating the practical needs of researchers and consultants into technical solutions;
collaborate with researchers, advisors and end users;
testing and improving existing systems;
thinking about innovations within the sector.

Your team

Within the Animal Farming Systems department, you will work together with a research team of 35 highly motivated project leaders, researchers and project assistants. We are known for our innovative and integrated approach in designing and evaluating the sustainability of animal farming systems. You will work together with colleagues from your own team and colleagues from other Wageningen Livestock Research departments or WUR research institutes in a project team.

This is where you will work

You will work on the greenest and most innovative campus in the Netherlands, and at a university that has been voted the "best university" in the Netherlands 20 times and is also seen worldwide as the best university in the agri-food domain.

Your qualities

You have analytical thinking skills and a solution-oriented mindset. In addition, you have good communication skills and a proactive attitude.

You Also Have

a completed bachelor focused on computer science, animal husbandry or agricultural entrepreneurship;
experience in developing software with e.g. C# or Python;
affinity with and interest in the livestock sector.

In our international working environment, communication is increasingly in English. This position involves language level (https://www.coe.int/en/web/common-european-framework-reference-languages/table-1-cefr-3.3-common-reference-levels-global-scale) C1. If you do not yet have this level, we will of course help you and you can contact our language center Wageningen in'to Language (https://www.wur.nl/nl/onderwijs-opleidingen/wageningen-into-languages.htm).

You can see that there are plenty of challenges for you. These challenges can also be seen as development opportunities. So if you do not yet have the track record required in the vacancy, but do have solid work experience, we would also like to invite you to apply.

We offer

Wageningen University & Research offers excellent terms of employment (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/conditions-of-employment). A few highlights from our Collective Labour Agreement include:

working hours that can be discussed and arranged so that they allow for the best possible work-life balance;
sabbatical leave, study leave, and partially paid parental leave;
there is a strong focus on vitality and you can make use of the sports facilities available on campus for a small fee;
a fixed year-end bonus of 8,3%;
excellent pension scheme.

In addition to these first-rate employee benefits, you will of course receive a good salary. We offer, depending on your experience, a competitive gross salary of between € 3,381.- and € 5,132.- for a full-time working week of 36 hours, in accordance with the CLA Wageningen Research (scale 8/9). Additionally, for this role a contract of 32 to 36 hours can be discussed. We initially offer a one-year contract, with the possibility of renewal subject to satisfactory performance and depending on the organisation’s financial situation.

We encourage development and internal mobility within our organisation. Our recruitment and selection policy sets out the conditions that apply specifically to you as a (former) employee. If you have any questions, we are happy to help.

Coming from abroad

WUR welcomes applications from international candidates. However, for applicants for this specific position from outside the EU/EFTA zone, immigration restrictions may apply based on Dutch and EU immigration laws. Such candidates may be eligible for an “ orientation year ” in the Netherlands or a visa as a “ knowledge migrant ”.

Wageningen University & Research is the university and research centre for life sciences. The themes we deal with are relevant to everyone around the world and Wageningen, therefore, has a large international community and a lot to offer to international employees.

Because we expect you to work and live in the Netherlands our team of advisors on Dutch immigration procedures will help you with the visa application procedures for yourself and, if applicable, for your family. If you come with a partner, we offer a Dual Career group program organized by our Welcome Center (https://wcfv.nl/en/home/global/our-services/happy-landing-and-living/). This program helps your partner to get familiar with the Dutch culture, labour market and assists your partner to find a job.

Feeling welcome also has everything to do with being well informed. Wageningen University & Research's International Community (https://www.wur.nl/en/jobs/expats-new-international-staff) page contains practical information about what we can do to support international employees coming to Wageningen. Furthermore, our Welcome Center can assist you with any additional advice and information about for example housing, opening a bank account or schooling. Finally, certain categories of international staff may be eligible for a tax exemption on a part of their salary during the first five years in the Netherlands.

Important information

For more information about the position, please contact ir. Frank Gort, Head of the Department of Animal Production Systems, via phone number: +31 681028847 or via email: frank.gort@wur.nl (mailto:frank.gort@wur.nl).

Questions about the procedure? Get in touch with Dax Teunissen, Corporate Recruiter, via email: recruitment.asg@wur.nl (mailto:recruitment.asg@wur.nl).

Ready to apply?

Click on the application button next to the vacancy on our website. Only applications submitted through our website will be considered.

You can apply up to and including Sunday September 27, 2026
. Internal candidates are preferred to apply before August 1, 2026.

Applications are reviewed regularly. Therefore, the position may be filled before the stated closing date.

Welcome, safe, and valued

Wageningen University & Research (WUR) highly values diversity and inclusion because we believe that different insights lead to innovative solutions. We create a work environment where everyone feels welcome, safe, and appreciated, regardless of background, identity, or experience. Together, we are building a culture where everyone's unique contribution adds to the success of our organization.

We are

The mission of Wageningen University & Research is “To explore the potential of nature to improve the quality of life”. Under the banner Wageningen University & Research, Wageningen University and the specialised research institutes of the Wageningen Research Foundation have joined forces in contributing to finding solutions to important questions in the domain of healthy food and living environment. With its roughly 30 branches, 7,600 employees (6,700 fte) and 13,100 students and over 150,000 participants to WUR’s Life Long Learning, Wageningen University & Research is one of the leading organisations in its domain. The unique Wageningen approach lies in its integrated approach to issues and the collaboration between different disciplines.

Read the 5 reasons (https://www.wur.nl/en/Jobs/Why-choose-WUR.htm) why your future colleagues enjoy working at WUR and watch the video below to get an idea of our green campus!

jobs.description:
BlueVi / Vacatures / Security Engineer

Deel vacature

Vacature

Security Engineer

HBO
32-40 uur
Hengelo, Eindhoven

Deel vacature

Bij BlueVi bewaak jij de security en privacy van een product dat dagelijks gezondheidsgegevens van meer dan 3,5 miljoen werknemers verwerkt. Dat vraagt om meer dan compliance op papier: security en privacy moeten in de kern van ons product zitten, en jij bent daar de technische eigenaar van. Dat gaat van secure coding tot risicobeoordeling, van incident response tot

certificering.

Wat ga je doen?

Je beoordeelt de technische risico’s van nieuwe features en verwerkingen, toetst DPIA’s, en

houdt ons vulnerability- en dependency-beleid scherp. Ook denk je actief mee over de tooling

die we daarvoor gebruiken, zoals Aikido. Je richt security monitoring en detectie in en bewaakt deze, en bent bij een incident of (vermeend) datalek het eerste aanspreekpunt; ook organiseer en volg je pentests op. Je bewaakt secure coding in onze PHP-, .NET- en Golang-codebases en houdt ons compliance-framework (ISO 27001, ISAE 3000, NEN-7510, AVG/GDPR) actueel.

Het hoge securityniveau dat we nastreven is een belangrijk deel van je werk. Je werkt in een multidisciplinair team met cloud- en devops engineers, waarmee je samen bouwt aan stabiele, schaalbare en veilige producten en Azure-infrastructuur. Ook de interne AI-ontwikkelingen, zoals ons gebruik van Azure AI Foundry, vallen binnen jouw aandachtsgebied. Een mooi terrein om als security engineer je stempel op te drukken.

Wie zoeken wij?

Je hebt hands-on ervaring met secure coding en code reviews (PHP, .NET en/of Golang), niet alleen vanuit een adviesrol.
Je hebt bij voorkeur gewerkt met gevoelige data, zoals in de medische sector (NEN-7510-kennis is een pluspunt) en kunt de technische inhoud van een DPIA beoordelen en toelichten.
Ook heb je eerder andere engineers getraind in of gecoacht op security best practices.
Engineers zijn je belangrijkste doelgroep, maar je durft ook de bredere organisatie mee te nemen in security bewustwording.
Je bent analytisch en pragmatisch, en net zo makkelijk zelf aan de code als in de rol van coach.

Wat bieden wij?

Je krijgt een rol met directe impact op ons product en de manier van werken van het engineering team, met de ruimte om mee te denken over tooling en de inrichting van ons securitybeleid.
Een aantrekkelijk salaris
Goede secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden,
Hybride werken vanuit Hengelo,
Een informeel, internationaal team dat security net zo serieus neemt als jij.

Over BlueVi

BlueVi helpt meer dan 3,5 miljoen werknemers veilig, gezond en duurzaam inzetbaar te houden. Dat doen wij door samen met onze klanten de meest flexibele, complete en gebruiksvriendelijke online-software en apps te ontwikkelen voor verzuimbegeleiding, verzuimpreventie, het verzekeren van inkomen en het inzetbaar houden van werknemers. Daarbij geloven wij sterk in de kracht van eenvoud, connectiviteit en data. Wij groeien sterk en zijn met meer dan 300.000 actieve gebruikers marktleider in Nederland. Vele grote en minder grote Nederlandse bedrijven gebruiken onze software en daar zijn we trots op.

Interesse?

Solliciteer direct, door middel van een motivatiebrief en CV, via het onderstaande formulier of hr@bluevi.com en we nemen graag contact met jou op. Staat de gewenste vacature er niet tussen, maar zou jij wel graag bij BlueVi aan de slag willen? Stuur dan jouw CV per e-mail naar hr@bluevi.com en wie weet wat we voor jou kunnen betekenen.

Are you looking to grow your career in software engineering? Join Social Security Scotland and help build digital services that make a real difference to people's lives across Scotland.

As an Associate Software Engineer, you'll work as part of a supportive and collaborative team, contributing to the development, maintenance and improvement of modern digital services. You'll have the opportunity to work with experienced engineers, learn new technologies, and develop your technical skills through hands-on experience, coaching and mentoring.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone at the early stages of their software engineering career who is keen to learn, solve problems and build high-quality digital solutions. You'll be supported to develop your knowledge across software development, testing, security, user-centred design and modern engineering practices, while gaining valuable experience working within a large public sector organisation.

At Social Security Scotland, continuous learning and professional development are encouraged. You'll have access to training, development opportunities and a clear pathway to progress your career within the Digital Profession. Whether you're building on existing experience or taking the next step in your career, you'll be part of a team that values collaboration, innovation and personal growth.

Together, we deliver digital services that are secure, accessible and user-focused, helping provide vital support to people across Scotland.

An Associate Software Engineer learns on the job by delivering software components.

At This Role Level, You Will

develop skills while working under supervision to deliver stories in a multidisciplinary team
understand and be proficient in different types of testing
be aware of but not responsible for security

Responsibilities

Support the development, testing, maintenance and improvement of software applications, services and infrastructure.
Assist in designing, building and documenting software components, programs and scripts, following established standards and guidance.
Work from user stories and requirements to help deliver solutions that meet user needs and improve user experience.
Contribute to system integration activities, including building and testing interfaces between systems.
Help identify, investigate and resolve software faults and technical issues using agreed processes and procedures.
Support the delivery of secure solutions by following information security requirements and applying security controls.
Assist with maintaining service availability, reliability and performance to ensure systems can meet expected demand.
Use prototyping techniques to explore ideas, test solutions and support development activities.
Collaborate with colleagues and wider project teams to contribute to the design and delivery of larger systems.
Apply modern software engineering standards, tools and practices, with support and guidance from experienced team members.

Success Profiles 

We use an assessment framework called ‘Success Profiles’ which lists the elements we test and provides detailed descriptions of each. Find out more about the framework here.

For this post, the following Success Profile elements will be assessed:

Experience

Experience of contributing to the development of low-complexity software components and working collaboratively as part of a wider team to deliver larger solutions.
Understanding of core Modern JavaScript Framework and/or AEM concepts, with the ability to deliver straightforward development tasks and user stories, seeking feedback and guidance where needed.

Behaviours

Communicating and Influencing (Level 2)
Working Together (Level 2)

You can find out more about Success Profiles Behaviours here:

Technical / Professional Skills

This role is aligned to Junior Developer
within the Government Digital and Data Profession.

These skills will be tested during the Technical Assessment if you are successful at sift stage. They will be not be assessed at application stage.

How To Apply 

Apply online, you must provide a CV and Supporting Statement (of no more than 750 words) which provides evidence of how you meet the Experience and Behaviours listed in the Success Profiles above. 

Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools can be used to support your application, but all statements and examples provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, and presented as your own) applications will be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action.

Please see our candidate guidance for more information on acceptable and unacceptable uses of AI in recruitment.

Should a large number of applications be received, an initial sift may be conducted using the CV and Supporting Statement against the first experience criteria. Candidates who pass the initial sift will have their applications fully assessed.

Please note there may be a telephone interview prior to the final interview stage.

Successful candidates will be invited to an interview which will assess the experience and behaviours, and a technical assessment comprising a technical question and answer session to assess the technical skills.

Full details of the interview and assessment process will be shared with shortlisted candidates once the sift has been completed.

We aim to provide feedback on request. However, if we receive a large number of applications it may not be possible for us to provide specific feedback on your application. We will provide feedback on request to candidates who attend an interview/assessment.

Sift - week commencing 5th October 2026

Interview – week commencing 19th October 2026

Location - In Person
in either Dundee or Glasgow

Social Security Scotland is an Executive Agency of the Scottish Government. Our benefits help people from all walks of life in Scotland. We offer rewarding careers and employ people across Scotland in a wide range of professions and roles. We are committed to recruiting a diverse workforce that is representative of the clients we serve.  Find more about us here.  

We offer a supportive and inclusive working environment along with a wide range of employee benefits. Find out more about what we offer. 

As part of the UK Civil Service, we uphold the Civil Service Nationality Rules.   

GDD Pay Supplement

This post is part of the Government Digital and Data (GDD) profession and currently attracts a £6,000 annual GDD pay supplement, which is paid monthly. Pay supplements are reviewed regularly.

Our standard hours are 35 hours per week and we offer a range of flexible working options, depending on the needs of the role. There is an expectation of a minimum 2 days per week in your assigned location, which will be either Glasgow or Dundee.  If you have specific questions about the role you are applying for, please contact us.

Successful candidates must complete the Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS), before they can be appointed. BPSS is comprised of four main pre-employment checks – Identity, Right to work, Employment History and a Criminal Record check (unspent convictions).

You can find out more about BPSS on the UK Government website, or read about the different levels of security checks in our Candidate Guide.
